flows.narrative: A new BofA/EPFR Flow Show edition for the week ended 30 Sep landed Friday morning UTC (2 Oct, 09:23 UTC) -- bonds out-earned equities for the week ($18.8bn vs $15.8bn global inflows), with a headline $118.0bn outflow from cash/money-market funds that is largely a mechanical quarter-end effect rather than a clean rotation into risk, since the amount leaving cash dwarfs what landed in the tracked equity/bond/gold/crypto buckets combined. Within bonds, long-duration (>6yr) government/corporate funds drew $7.4bn (the best since May 2025) and municipal bond funds set a record $4.2bn weekly inflow -- a clear duration-buying bid. Within equities, the US saw a second straight week of outflows (-$2.7bn) even as China (+$3.7bn, best in 9 weeks), Japan (+$1.8bn, 6th straight week) and EM broadly (+$3.2bn, inflows resumed) all drew fresh money, and US-listed tech funds alone pulled in $3.3bn (best in 5 weeks) -- so the US picture is a split between broad outflows and a narrow mega-cap/AI-tech bid. BofA's own Bull & Bear sentiment indicator eased to 8.8 from 9.3, still deep in the contrarian 'Sell' zone (>8) but off its most extreme recent reading. ICI's separate weekly mutual-fund/ETF print has not advanced past the week ended 23 Sep ($20.14bn combined long-term fund + ETF inflows, of which equity funds were +$12.88bn) -- its next release (week ended 30 Sep) is due ~7 Oct, several days out, so it is carried forward unchanged while the BofA/EPFR leg above is freshly updated.
